bioprojects.title: Genome sequencing of the Anopheles gambiae molecular form M strain

assembly_info.comments:
Source of sequence data: Washington University Genome Sequencing Center.
Source of DNA used for sequencing: Nora Besansky, University of Notre Dame, Notre Dame IN 46556-0369. The DNA was purified from the Anopheles gambiae Mali-NIH colony, available through MR4. Collected in a village near Niono, Mali in June 2005. Established by combining ca. 80 isofemale families that were molecularly identified as A.gambiae M molecular form and karyotyped as 2Rbc/bc; 2La/a. DNA source for plasmid library was adult males; for fosmid and BAC libraries it was pupae of mixed sexes. Total sequence traces comprise 94% plasmid reads (5-6kb inserts), 4% fosmid reads (40kb inserts), and 2% BAC ends (120 kb inserts).
The ABKP01000000 version of this project included low-coverage degenerates from the many minor variant haplotypes in the sequenced population. Those low-coverage degenerates were excluded from this version of the project, ABKP02000000.
Long-term curation of the sequence and subsequent annotation updates is the responsibility of VectorBase at http://www.vectorbase.org.
This version of the assembly, m5, represents 8x coverage of the genome.

The VEuPathDB Bioinformatics Resource Center (www.veupathdb.org) is responsible for the assembled genome sequence and its annotation as of March 2022. Annotation and related data can be viewed and updated at http://veupathdb.org and inquiries can be sent to help@veupathdb.org.
